stories.headline: NASA Launches Artemis II, First Crewed Lunar Mission in 53 Years, Sending Four Astronauts Around the Moon

key_facts.fact: Artemis II launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT (2235 GMT) on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center, carrying four astronauts on a nearly 10-day mission around the moon.
key_facts.excerpt: Four astronauts blasted off from Florida on Wednesday on NASA's Artemis II mission... The 32-story-tall space vehicle thundered into clear skies trailing a towering column of thick, white vapor.

key_facts.fact: The crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, plus Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — the first woman, Black astronaut, and Canadian ever flown to the moon.
key_facts.excerpt: the crew consisting of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, plus Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, will fly around the moon and back

key_facts.fact: The mission will send the crew 252,000 miles into space, farther than humans have ever traveled, surpassing Apollo 13's record of roughly 248,000 miles set in 1970.
key_facts.excerpt: The Artemis II mission will send its four-person crew some 252,000 miles (406,000 km) into space — the farthest humans have ever traveled.

key_facts.fact: It is the world's first mission to send astronauts in the vicinity of the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972, a gap of 53 years.
key_facts.excerpt: the world's first to send astronauts in the vicinity of the moon, out of Earth's orbit, in 53 years

key_facts.fact: The mission serves as a dress rehearsal for Artemis IV, targeting a first-ever landing of astronauts on the moon's South Pole in 2028, aiming to beat China's planned crewed lunar mission as early as 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA is targeting 2028 for Artemis IV, a first-ever landing of astronauts on the moon's South Pole, seeking to beat China's planned crewed mission to the same lunar region as early as 2030.

key_facts.fact: The SLS rocket's upper stage successfully separated from the Lockheed Martin Orion capsule; the crew then manually steered the spacecraft around the upper stage to demonstrate maneuverability.
key_facts.excerpt: the SLS rocket's upper stage successfully separated from the Lockheed Martin-made Orion capsule... The crew then began work on an early test objective: manually steering the spacecraft around the upper stage

key_facts.fact: The SLS program has an estimated cost of $2 billion to $4 billion per launch; NASA lost roughly 20% of its workforce under federal downsizing efforts last year.
key_facts.excerpt: a program partly known for its ballooning costs at an estimated $2 billion to $4 billion per launch... a space agency that lost roughly 20% of its workforce under the Trump administration's federal downsizing efforts last year

stories.headline: SpaceX Files Confidentially for IPO Targeting $1.75T+ Valuation, Could Raise Record $75B

key_facts.fact: SpaceX submitted a confidential draft registration to the SEC for an IPO that could happen as early as June 2026, with a valuation exceeding $1.75 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is preparing to go public, having submitted a confidential draft registration for an initial stock offering to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission... the listing could happen as soon as June, with a valuation that may exceed $1.75 trillion.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX aims to raise up to $75 billion, which would surpass Saudi Aramco's $29 billion debut in 2019, the largest IPO on record.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX aims to raise up to $75 billion — an offering that would surpass Saudi Aramco's $29 billion debut in 2019, the largest IPO on record.

key_facts.fact: Bank of America, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, with Barclays, Deutsche Bank, UBS, RBC, and Mizuho handling regional orders.
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of America, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, and Morgan Stanley have senior roles on the offering... Barclays is handling U.K. orders. Deutsche Bank and UBS are working on European orders.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is considering a dual-class stock structure for insider voting power and may allocate up to 30% of the offering to retail investors.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is considering a dual-class stock structure to give insiders, including founder Elon Musk, extra voting power. The company may allocate up to 30% of the stock offering to retail investors.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX merged with Musk's xAI in February; SpaceX revenue is approaching $20 billion in 2026 while xAI is expected to contribute less than $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX merged with Musk's artificial intelligence startup xAI in February... SpaceX's revenue — approaching $20 billion in 2026 — while xAI is expected to contribute less than $1 billion

key_facts.fact: If the IPO reaches its target, Musk would be the first person to lead two publicly traded companies each worth over $1 trillion (SpaceX and Tesla at ~$1.4T).
key_facts.excerpt: If the IPO reaches its target valuation, Musk will be the first person to lead two publicly traded companies each worth over $1 trillion.

stories.headline: Trump Says Iran War Objectives 'Nearing Completion,' Threatens NATO Exit as Markets Reverse

key_facts.fact: In a prime-time address to the nation on April 1, Trump said Iran war 'core strategic objectives are nearing completion,' citing degradation of Iran's missiles, drones, and navy.
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump gave an update on the Iran war Wednesday night, saying the operation's 'core strategic objectives are nearing completion,' citing the degradation of the country's missiles, drones and navy.

key_facts.fact: Trump said the US will hit Iran 'extremely hard' over the next two to three weeks and will complete its military mission 'very shortly.'
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. will complete its military mission in Iran 'very shortly,' Mr. Trump said, adding that they will hit Iran 'extremely hard' over the next two to three weeks.

key_facts.fact: Trump signaled the US would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying countries that rely on it 'must take care of that passage' and 'grab it and cherish it.'
key_facts.excerpt: he could end U.S. operations without reopening the Strait of Hormuz, leaving other countries to deal with Tehran's chokehold on the critical shipping lane. In his prime-time address, the president said countries that heavily rely on the strait 'must take care of that passage' and 'grab it and cherish it.'

key_facts.fact: Trump told Britain's Telegraph he could attempt to pull the US out of NATO, frustrated at allies for declining to join the US-Israeli war on Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Trump has told Britain's Telegraph newspaper he could attempt to pull the U.S. out of the transatlantic NATO alliance it's led for more than seven decades, as he vents frustration at America's closest allies for declining to join the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

key_facts.fact: Crude oil futures spiked more than 5% after Trump's speech while stock futures slid, reversing an earlier rally that had been driven by hopes the war might conclude soon.
key_facts.excerpt: Crude oil futures spiked more than 5% after the president's speech while stock futures slid, reversing a drop in oil prices and a stock market rally from earlier in the day amid hopes that the war might conclude soon.

key_facts.fact: Earlier on April 1, Trump claimed Iran's president had asked for a ceasefire; Tehran denied the claim.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Trump said earlier Wednesday that Iran wants a ceasefire

stories.headline: Iranian Strike Damages Amazon AWS Data Center in Bahrain, Second Disruption in a Month

key_facts.fact: Amazon's cloud computing operation in Bahrain was damaged after an Iranian strike on April 1, according to the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's cloud computing operation in Bahrain was damaged after an Iranian strike, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said civil defence teams were extinguishing a fire at a company facility following what authorities described as an Iranian attack.
key_facts.excerpt: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said earlier in the day that civil defence teams were extinguishing a fire at a company facility following what authorities described as an Iranian attack.

key_facts.fact: The strike came a day after Iran's Revolutionary Guards threatened to target 18 US companies in the Middle East, including Microsoft, Google, and Apple, in retaliation for attacks on Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: The report of the strike came a day after Iran's Revolutionary Guards threatened to target U.S. companies in the Middle East, including Microsoft, Google and Apple, in retaliation for attacks on Iran.

key_facts.fact: This is the second time in a month that AWS operations in Bahrain have been affected by the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, the e-commerce giant said its Amazon Web Services region in Bahrain had been 'disrupted' amid the current conflict in the Middle East, marking the second time in a month that its operations have been affected by the war.

key_facts.fact: AWS Bahrain and UAE regions have essentially been non-functional since early March, with Amazon not providing updates since March 3.

stories.headline: IEA Warns April Oil Losses Will Double, Calls Current Crisis Worst in History at 12M Barrels Per Day Lost

key_facts.fact: IEA Chief Fatih Birol said April oil losses will be twice the loss of March, as cargo ships that transited the Strait of Hormuz before the war have now been depleted.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The next month, April, will be much worse than March,' he said... 'In April, there is nothing. The loss of oil in April will be twice the loss of oil in March.'

key_facts.fact: The current crisis has caused a loss of 12 million barrels per day — more than the 1973 and 1979 oil crises combined, which each lost about 5 million bpd.
key_facts.excerpt: 'When you look at the [1973 and 1979], in both of them we lost each about 5 million barrels per day of oil... Today, we lost 12 million barrels per day — more than two of these oil crises put together.'

key_facts.fact: The IEA is weighing another release of strategic oil reserves after member countries already released a record 400 million barrels in March.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are assessing the market on a daily, if not hourly, basis, 24/7. If we think there is a need, we may well make a suggestion [to release more reserves]'... the IEA's 32 member countries agreed to release a record 400 million barrels of oil

key_facts.fact: Brent crude surged more than 60% in March, the biggest monthly price gain since records began in the 1980s; Axios reported oil could hit $200/barrel if Hormuz remains closed.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the course of March, global benchmark Brent crude oil surged more than 60%, marking the biggest monthly price gain since records began in the 1980s.

key_facts.fact: Birol identified jet fuel and diesel as the biggest shortages, already hitting Asia with impacts expected in Europe by April or early May.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The biggest problem today is the lack of jet fuel and diesel; these are the main challenges and we are seeing it already in Asia, but soon, in April, or maybe beginning of May, it will come to Europe.'

key_facts.fact: Birol called the current crisis the biggest energy disruption in history, exceeding the combined impact of three previous major crises including the 2022 Russian gas disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The current crisis is more than all these three put together. Plus, in addition to this, there are many vital commodities — petrochemicals, fertilizers, sulfur — they are very important for the global supply chains... We are heading towards a major, major disruption, and the biggest in history.'

stories.headline: FDA Approves Eli Lilly's Foundayo, First Oral Non-Peptide GLP-1 Pill for Weight Loss at $149/Month

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) on April 1 for adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related medical problems, making it the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight loss.
key_facts.excerpt: Eli Lilly and Company today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Foundayo (orforglipron) for adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related medical problems.

key_facts.fact: In the ATTAIN-1 trial, patients on the highest dose lost an average of 27.3 pounds (12.4% body weight) compared to 2.2 pounds (0.9%) with placebo over 72 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: individuals taking the highest dose of Foundayo and who stayed on treatment lost an average of 27.3 pounds (12.4%) compared to 2.2 pounds (0.9%) with placebo.

key_facts.fact: Foundayo can be taken any time of day without food or water restrictions, a key advantage over competing oral GLP-1 treatments.
key_facts.excerpt: the only GLP-1 pill for weight loss that can be taken any time of day without food or water restrictions

key_facts.fact: Pricing starts at $25/month with commercial insurance and $149/month for self-pay; available via LillyDirect starting April 6, then retail pharmacies.
key_facts.excerpt: Eligible people with commercial insurance may pay as little as $25 per month... Individuals opting for self-pay can access Foundayo starting at $149 per month... shipping beginning April 6

key_facts.fact: The drug was discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical and licensed by Lilly in 2018; it is Lilly's second FDA-approved obesity medicine alongside injectable Zepbound (tirzepatide).
key_facts.excerpt: Foundayo, Lilly's second FDA-approved obesity medicine... Orforglipron was discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and licensed by Lilly in 2018.

key_facts.fact: Lilly has submitted orforglipron for weight management and/or type 2 diabetes in more than 40 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Lilly has submitted orforglipron for weight management and/or type 2 diabetes in more than 40 countries and plans to launch in each country shortly after approval.

stories.headline: Chinese Chipmakers Capture 41% of China's AI Server Market as Nvidia's Share Erodes to 55%

key_facts.fact: Chinese GPU and AI chip makers shipped 1.65 million cards in 2025, capturing 41% of China's AI accelerator server market, according to IDC data reviewed by Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese vendors collectively shipped 1.65 million cards, accounting for 41% of the total market — a milestone that underscores how aggressively domestic players have moved to fill the void left by tightening U.S. export controls.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia remained market leader with ~2.2 million cards shipped (55% share), but this marks a significant retreat from its once-dominant position. AMD held 4% with 160,000 cards.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia remained the market leader, shipping around 2.2 million cards and holding a 55% share. But that figure marks a significant retreat... AMD carved out a modest presence, shipping roughly 160,000 cards for a 4% share

key_facts.fact: Huawei leads Chinese vendors with ~812,000 AI chips shipped (roughly half of all domestic shipments), followed by Alibaba's T-Head with 265,000 cards.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei Technologies emerged as the runaway leader among Chinese vendors, shipping around 812,000 AI chips, roughly half of all domestically branded shipments. Alibaba's chip design unit T-Head claimed second place, shipping approximately 265,000 cards.

key_facts.fact: Total shipments of AI accelerator cards across all vendors reached approximately 4 million units in China in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Total shipments of AI accelerator cards by Nvidia, AMD, and Chinese chipmakers reached approximately 4 million units in China in 2025

key_facts.fact: Beijing's central government launched a new wave of AI infrastructure spending in 2025, with local governments accelerating intelligent computing centers carrying implicit directives to 'buy Chinese.'
key_facts.excerpt: the central government launched a new wave of AI infrastructure spending, with local governments accelerating intelligent computing centers across provinces, many of which carried implicit directives to 'buy Chinese.'

stories.headline: Solana DeFi Platform Drift Protocol Suffers $270M+ Exploit via Compromised Admin Key

key_facts.fact: Drift Protocol, a decentralized exchange on Solana, confirmed an active attack on April 1, with over $270 million in assets transferred to a suspicious wallet.
key_facts.excerpt: a popular trading venue on the solana blockchain, Drift, is suffering from an ongoing... $270M

key_facts.fact: The attacker swapped stolen assets into USDC, then bridged to Ethereum to buy ETH; by the time of tracking, 19,913 ETH ($42.6 million) had been purchased.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift Protocol Hack: $270M Exploit as Attacker Bridges Funds to Ethereum and Buys ETH

key_facts.fact: The exploit reportedly stemmed from a single compromised admin key; the attacker returned for additional funds two hours after the initial hack.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift Protocol Suffers ~$280M Exploit; attacker used pre-signed durable-nonce transactions and social engineering

key_facts.fact: Drift suspended all deposits and withdrawals and said it was coordinating with multiple security firms, bridges, and exchanges to contain the incident.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift Protocol is experiencing an active attack. Deposits and withdrawals have been suspended.

key_facts.fact: The exploit is one of the largest DeFi hacks of 2026, with total losses estimated between $270M and $285M.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift Protocol hack drains up to $285M

key_facts.fact: The compromised system contained pen register and trap-and-trace surveillance returns — data showing who communicated with whom under active FBI investigations.

key_facts.fact: A 'major incident' designation means the breach poses significant risks to U.S. national security and triggers mandatory notification to Congress and other federal oversight bodies.
